description: _run_fallback (line 1059) returns None for ANY failure of the fallback endpoint (connection error, non-200, non-JSON), and _request returns that None at line 1044 as if it were a successful payload. The sole caller _search_full (line 2010) immediately executes `diag = _query_diag(data)` and `data.get(...)` with data=None, raising AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get' at line 2011. Trigger: mode='local' with a key lacking local support that returns a retryable status (429/5xx/404) on the local endpoint while the web fallback GET also fails. The docs promise 'Local mode can fall back to web search; inspect `fallback`' (references/api.md line 96) — instead the whole search crashes.
suggestion: In _request, when `fallback` is set and `_run_fallback` returns None, raise the original classified error (`error`) instead of returning None.

description: _summarizer fallback path builds a malformed deep link: 'https://search.brave.com/summarizer?key=' + _up.urlencode({'key': key}) produces '...summarizer?key=key=%3C...%3E' (the literal 'key=' prefix is doubled because urlencode already emits the key name). The success path at line 1776 correctly uses '?' + urlencode without the hardcoded 'key='. Any string key that fails json.loads (or parses to a non-dict, e.g. a string, triggering AttributeError at line 1769) hits this branch and yields a broken link.
suggestion: Use the same construction as line 1776: 'https://search.brave.com/summarizer?' + _up.urlencode({'key': key})

description: `if isinstance(data, dict) or data is not None:` is a tautology equivalent to `if data is not None:` (a dict is never None). So the intended '200-but-unparseable is a server-side oddity; treat as transient' path (lines 1017-1025) is unreachable: resp.json() that parses to None (literal 'null'), a bare JSON string, number, or list is returned as the payload. Any downstream `data.get(...)` (e.g. _query_diag at line 1716) then crashes with AttributeError/TypeError on a non-dict 'successful' response.
suggestion: Use `if isinstance(data, dict):` so non-dict/None 200 bodies fall through to the retry/raise path as the comment intends.

description: `if fallback and resp.status_code != 200 and (retryable or not fast_fail and fallback is not None):` — `and` binds tighter than `or`, so the condition is `... and (retryable or ((not fast_fail) and (fallback is not None)))`. `fallback is not None` is always true here (first clause of the chain), making the inner `and` dead; and a fast-fail status that is also retryable (e.g. a 429 body tagged component=authentication) silently takes the fallback, inverting the 'definitive errors are not retried/fallen-back' contract stated in the docstring (lines 975-976).
suggestion: Explicitly parenthesise: `if fallback and resp.status_code != 200 and (retryable or not fast_fail):` and drop the redundant `fallback is not None` (and possibly the _fallback_ok stub).

description: In the default call (max_age_hours=None), `fetch([result_r.url], max_characters=text_cap, include_sections=["body"], text_verbosity="standard", max_age_hours=None)` hits fetch()'s backward-compat single-URL string branch (fetch lines 1823-1832: condition `len(results)==1 and mode=="text" and not(with_highlights or with_summary) and not extras_links and max_age_hours is None` is all True, and it does not account for include_sections/text_verbosity). So `body` is a `str`, not a list. The `isinstance(body, list)` check at line 4456 is then False, so website_url/website_title/website_text are NEVER added, and no website_error is set either. The docstring promises these fields on a successful fetch_website, but the normal success path returns a dict without them.
suggestion: Pass include_meta=True (fetch then returns an envelope with 'results'), or force a non-None max_age_hours, or make fetch() treat include_sections/text_verbosity as 'rich options' that disable the string form. Then read body['results'][0]['text'].

description: The deprecation gate regex r"\b(deprecat|obsolete|removed|migrat|breaking|sunset)\b" (also 5800, and the shaded copies 5550/5554/5567) requires a word boundary on BOTH sides of each stem. Since 'deprecat', 'remov', 'migrat' are stems, not whole words, \bdeprecat\b only matches the literal non-word 'deprecat'. Verified: it fails to match 'deprecated', 'deprecation', 'deprecating', 'removed', 'removal', 'migration', 'migrating' — i.e. the actual deprecation vocabulary — while only catching whole words 'obsolete', 'removed', 'breaking', 'sunset', 'end of life'. _dep_type() (substring, no \b) would classify 'deprecated' fine, but items never reach it because this gate rejects them first. Net effect: deprecations() returns near-empty signals/counts for its primary use case.
suggestion: Drop the trailing \b (keep leading \b only) or use substring matching: r"\b(deprecat|obsolet|end[- ]of[- ]life|remov|migrat|breaking|sunset)" so stems match as prefixes.

description: _get_api_key returns _API_KEY_CACHE[label] before ever re-reading the environment. Once a key has been resolved, a corrected EXA_API_KEY re-exported in the same long-lived process (exactly the recovery the ExaAuthError message on line 528 tells the user to do: 'export a fresh EXA_API_KEY') is ignored and the stale key keeps producing 401s forever. There is no cache-invalidation or re-check path anywhere in the module.
suggestion: Prefer the live environment variable over the cache (cache only file-derived keys, or re-run _seek_api_key when os.environ.get(_API_KEY_NAMES[0]) differs from the cached value).

description: The `now` parameter (documented in the docstring as an optional datetime override, 'mostly for tests') is silently ignored. Line 3481 reassigns `now = datetime.now(tz) if tz else datetime.now()`, shadowing the caller-supplied value. Any test or caller passing `now=some_datetime` gets the current time instead, making the override a no-op.
suggestion: Replace line 3481 with: `if now is None: now = datetime.now(tz) if tz else datetime.now()` so the parameter is honoured when provided.

description: research() emits the key 'summary_dead_link' but its docstring (line 2265) and the summarizer machinery (deep_link built in _summarizer, line 1776) promise 'summary_deep_link'. 'dead' is a typo of 'deep', so the summarizer deep-link is unreachable under its documented name and any caller doing result['summary_deep_link'] gets KeyError.
suggestion: Rename the returned key at line 2345 to 'summary_deep_link'.

description: webset_items_all uses a 'while True' that keeps appending to 'items' and advancing cursor until hasMore is false. There is no duplicate-page / progress guard: if the API ever repeats a cursor or keeps hasMore true, the loop is infinite and the list grows without bound. Same class of risk applies to webset_snapshot which holds the full list in memory.
suggestion: Add a safety bound (max pages, or stop when a nextCursor repeats) to prevent infinite pagination.

description: _mode_args raises a plain ValueError for an unknown mode, while every other validation in this section (and the module) raises ExaError. The ExaError docstring explicitly covers 'an invalid option combo is given', so a caller doing `except ExaError` around search()/run() will NOT catch a bad mode and will get an unhandled ValueError instead.
suggestion: Raise ExaError (or a dedicated subclass) for unknown mode to match the rest of the module.

description: answer() accepts and forwards an undocumented `stream` parameter (declared line 1900, not in the Args docstring) into body["stream"] (line 1939), but routes through _request() which does resp.json(). When stream=True the /answer endpoint returns an SSE stream (as stream_answer at line 2642 confirms by posting stream=True and parsing SSE lines), so resp.json() raises an uncaught httpx/JSON decode error instead of returning an Answer. Passing stream=True to answer() crashes with an obscure error; the documented streaming path is stream_answer().
suggestion: Either document/validate stream (raise a clear error directing the user to stream_answer when stream=True) or parse the SSE stream; simplest is to reject stream=True with an ExaError pointing to stream_answer().

description: The legacy string-form guard checks only `not extras_links and max_age_hours is None` (line 1824), ignoring the other rich extras (extras_image_links, extras_rich_links, extras_rich_image_links, extras_code_blocks) and other rich options (text_verbosity, subpages, include_sections, highlights_max_characters). So a single-URL text fetch such as fetch(urls=[u], extras_code_blocks=5) still returns the plain '--- Title ---\n<body>' string and silently discards the requested structured extras, contradicting the docstring promise that the string form is used only 'when no rich options are requested'.
suggestion: Make the guard cover all rich options (any extras_*, text_verbosity, subpages>0, subpage_target, include_sections, etc.) so the structured list is returned whenever a rich option is actually requested.

description: Answer.__init__ sets self.citations = raw.get("citations", []) (line 1854). If the /answer API returns the key with a null value ("citations": null) the default is not applied, so citations becomes None; Answer.sources (line 1860), to_dict (line 1866), to_markdown (line 1879) and __repr__ (line 1891) then raise TypeError ('NoneType' not iterable / not a len()). The sibling stream_answer defensively normalizes with `obj.get("citations") or []` (line 2672), confirming empty/absent citations is a real response shape, so Answer should use the same guard.
suggestion: Use self.citations = raw.get("citations") or [] to mirror stream_answer and avoid the None crash.

description: agent() early-returns a terminal run created already terminal (`if run.done: return run`) without running the `raise_on_failed` check at line 2425. If POST /agent/runs returns a run that is already `failed` (rare per the comment, but e.g. an instantly-failing continuation), the default `raise_on_failed=True` contract documented in the docstring (lines 2368-2369, 2375-2377) is violated: a failed AgentRun is silently returned instead of raising ExaError, unlike the poll path which does raise.
suggestion: Move/apply the `if raise_on_failed and run.status == "failed": raise` check after the early return as well (check both the pre-poll and post-poll run objects).

description: The docstring says `timeout` is the 'Max total wall-clock seconds to wait for completion' (line 2366), but `deadline = time.time() + timeout` is computed AFTER the create call at line 2404, which itself runs with `timeout=min(timeout, 30)`; each in-flight poll GET at line 2412 also carries `timeout=min(timeout, 45)`. Total elapsed wall-clock can therefore exceed `timeout` by up to ~30s (create) + up to ~45s (one in-flight poll) for default timeout=120, and for small timeouts (e.g. timeout=10) the actual wait can be roughly double the promised bound.
suggestion: Subtract elapsed time from the create call before computing the deadline (e.g. record t0 before POST and use `deadline = t0 + timeout`), and/or cap the per-poll request timeout by remaining time.

description: top_terms() docstring (lines 1007-1008) promises domain_clusters entries shaped {"domain","results"} but the actual key returned is "count" ({"domain": d, "count": c}). Downstream code or skill instructions following the documented shape get KeyError on 'results'.
suggestion: Either rename the returned key to 'results' or fix the docstring to 'count'.

description: entity_search() accepts dedupe: bool = True but never reads it; deduplication always happens, so dedupe=False still dedupes - a silent contract violation for callers who pass it.
suggestion: Honor dedupe=False (skip roster dedup, keep all records) or drop the parameter.

description: monitor_create's `timeout=45.0` keyword is accepted (line 2934) but never used; the request hardcodes timeout=30. A caller passing timeout=120 gets a 30s request that can raise httpx.TimeoutException earlier than requested, and the default is also not the documented 45s.
suggestion: Pass timeout=timeout to _request (or drop the parameter).

description: monitor_check docstring promises a dict with 'latest_run' (and references nonexistent parameter 'auto_if_empty' at line 3114); the actual returns are {monitor_id, has_run, run_id, run_output, triggered} with no 'latest_run' key in either branch (lines 3123-3129, 3135-3141). Callers keying off documented fields get KeyError/None.
suggestion: Add 'latest_run' (the full run dict) to both return dicts or fix the docstring; rename auto_if_empty to trigger_if_empty.

description: monitor_check triggers a new run whenever runs_data[0] has no output, even when an older completed run with output exists, and even while a run is in progress. Docstring (line 3103) and jobs.md say it should only trigger when the monitor has NO completed run, so e.g. runs=[running, completed-with-output] triggers a duplicate/paid run contrary to documented semantics.
suggestion: Scan the fetched runs for a completed run with output first; only trigger if none exists (and ideally skip if latest is still 'running').

description: webset_eval_review's docstring (lines 3668-3669) promises keys 'item_count' and 'by_satisfied', but the actual return (lines 3697-3698) uses 'count' and 'by_satisfaction'. Any caller following the documented shape gets KeyError on result['item_count'] or result['by_satisfied'].
suggestion: Rename the returned keys to match the docstring (item_count, by_satisfied) or update the docstring to 'count'/'by_satisfaction'.

description: Five functions are defined twice in this range; the first definition of each is shadowed and never executed at runtime (module dict keeps the last binding). Pairs: pkg_releases 5459->5705, _dep_type 5507->5753, deprecations 5522->5768, snippet 5581->5826, code_lint_tips 5672->5870. The 5459/5507/5522/5581/5672 copies (plus the duplicated banner comment at 5450-5456 and 5696-5702) are dead. This is ~200 lines of duplicated code and a maintenance hazard (any future edit must be applied to two places).
suggestion: Delete the first (shaded) copies at 5459, 5507, 5522, 5581, 5672 and the duplicate banner comment at 5450-5456, keeping only the effective 5705/5753/5768/5826/5870 block and the single banner.

description: Missing key raises a bare RuntimeError, but the ExaAuthError docstring (lines 382-383) says it covers 'the API key is missing, invalid, or revoked' and references/usage.md tells users to catch ExaAuthError for auth problems. Callers following the docs and catching ExaAuthError will miss the missing-key case entirely.
suggestion: Raise ExaAuthError (or document RuntimeError explicitly) for the not-configured case so the documented catch set works.

description: stream_answer's docstring documents the trailing meta dict as "cost_dollars": {...} (an object), and the rest of the module treats cost as a dict (e.g. costDollars.total, SearchResults.total_cost). But the code (line 2675) collapses it to the scalar float (obj.get('costDollars') or {}).get('total'), so the yielded dict actually carries cost_dollars as a float/None.
suggestion: Either emit the raw costDollars dict to match the doc/module convention, or fix the docstring example to show a scalar; a caller that does meta['cost_dollars']['total'] per the documented shape raises TypeError/AttributeError.

description: `d.get("pronounciation")` uses a misspelled key. If the Brave API returns the correctly-spelled key `"pronunciation"`, the `pronunciation` field in the normalised output will always be None. The docstring for `_rich_definitions` lists `pronunciation` as a returned field.
suggestion: Change to `d.get("pronunciation")` (or use a fallback: `d.get("pronunciation") or d.get("pronounciation")`) after verifying the actual API response key.

description: rich() docstring (lines 4073-4074) promises the package always contains "render" and "raw", but the early-return path at lines 4085-4087 (no callback_key, or fetch=False) omits both keys. SKILL.md/verticals.md say no-hint is a normal outcome, so consumers doing out["raw"] or out["render"] on a hintless query raise KeyError. Two return shapes for one function.
suggestion: Always include "render" (empty string) and "raw" ({}) in the early return, or document that the keys are absent on the hint-only path.

description: The typed helpers weather/stock_quote/crypto/definition/currency_x/convert_values (lines 4220-4251) blindly return rich() output without checking that the hint's vertical actually matches the requested subtype. Their docstrings promise results[0]["data"] is the specific normalised block, but if the hint maps to a different vertical (e.g. stock_quote("apple") returning a definitions vertical) or returns no hint at all, callers silently get wrong-vertical or empty data with no warning.
suggestion: In each helper, compare result["vertical"] (or results[0]["subtype"]) to the expected subtype and either return a flagged/empty package or at least note the mismatch.

description: In drinks(), `dom = (r.get("domain") or "").lower()` reads a `domain` key off the web result item `r`. Web items are normalized by _web_item (line 1283) which has NO `domain` key (its site field is `site`), so r.get("domain") is always None and dom is always "". The domain-based drink heuristic `any(s in dom for s in ("liquor","cocktail","drink","wine"))` therefore never fires, contrary to the documented intent (docstring lines 3201-3203: "whose title/domain signals a cocktail"). Drink recipes that would otherwise be caught via their source host are silently dropped, yielding an under-sized results set.
suggestion: Use the web item's site host `r.get("site")` (or the recipe block's domain `rc.get("domain")` if that is what was meant) instead of the nonexistent `r.get("domain")`.

description: software()'s docstring (line 2381) documents the return key as `"registries":{pypi->[names], npm->[names]}`, but the actual returned dict uses the key `"registry"` (line 2419). A caller following the documented contract does res["registries"] and gets KeyError. Relatedly, the docstring says `versions` is `[version str...]` while the code returns a list of dicts {name,version,url,code} (line 2398).
suggestion: Rename the returned key to `registries` to match the docstring, or correct the docstring to `registry`; also fix the `versions` doc description to list-of-dicts.

description: research() computes 'duplicates' as sum(p['n'] for p in per_search if p['n']) - len(out_items). Each per-query 'n' equals the count of items actually appended to out_items for that query, so the sum always equals len(out_items) and 'duplicates' is always 0. It never reflects the URLs actually dropped during cross-query dedup (the value the docstring 'duplicates: int' implies).
suggestion: Track the raw pre-dedup count per query and subtract the kept count, or compute duplicates from a seen-set hit counter rather than the appended count.
